findings.reason: splitting §65 into two sections lets each be dispatched, gated and closed on its own result, which is how this plan handled the same two-results-in-one-section defect for §54 and §57.
findings.text: §65's heading ("reuses the events-path owner and tests its newest-transition choice") and Deliverable state two results that close independently: routing the other-project scan through `watch_stream_path` and removing the duplicate suffix constant (a source change in recovery_watch.py), and publishing C's producer live so the project-C clause depends on the newest-transition selection (a change to tests/test_a_pane_counts_its_session_across_projects.py); a coordinator cannot close the node on one verdict, because the dedup can land while the clause still cannot fail, or the clause can be fixed while the duplicate spelling remains

findings.reason: requiring the same grep run first at the node's base (as §58 was repaired to do) makes the removal provable rather than an unverified empty result.
findings.text: the done-when's "A `git grep -n '\.events"' reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py` at the delivered head prints nothing" records an absence as proof of removal but names no control showing the pattern finds anything; at the node's base the pattern matches exactly one line (recovery_watch.py:2067), so a mistyped or mis-scoped pattern would print nothing at the delivered head whether or not the constant was removed
